title: What does VaultCreate do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of VaultCreate and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, VaultCreate establishes a single-asset vault and its share-accounting structure. [1]

Participants deposit an eligible asset and receive shares under the vault's rules. The vault and its pseudo-account have distinct ledger roles. Creating a vault does not prove a profitable strategy or guaranteed redemption liquidity. Review its asset, permissions and management configuration before using shares as evidence of a fixed amount of underlying funds. [1]

The VaultCreate reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using VaultCreate, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
